title: Trace and base-change rearrangement before the second triangle
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$. Schemes are separated finite-type $k$-schemes and morphisms are $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Write $R_Z=\mathcal O_{E,Z}$ for the pulled-back condensed coefficient ring, $D(Z)=D(\Mod_{R_Z})$ for its unbounded derived category [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], and $\mathcal L(Z)=\Loc(\Dbc(Z,\mathcal O_E))$ [sk-def-sfb-constructible, sk-def-localizing-closure]. Pullbacks and direct images are the canonical derived functors with adjunction $h^*\dashv Rh_*$ [def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull-adjunction], and pullback coefficients are identified by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. All tensors are derived tensors over $R_Z$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. For a proper $h:Z\to B$, let $\pi_{h,L,N}:L\otimes Rh_*N\to Rh_*(h^*L\otimes N)$ be the canonical projection map, the adjoint transpose of $1\otimes c_{h,N}$, where $c_h$ is the canonical counit.

Let $f:X\to Y$ be proper, let $W=X\times_YX$ with projections $p_1,p_2$ [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], and use the canonical identification $fp_1=fp_2$. Put $T_Y=R_Y(1)[2]$, $T_X=f^*T_Y$, and $T_W=p_1^*T_X=p_2^*T_X$, with twists as in [sk-def-sp-tate-twist] and pullback/tensor comparisons as in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Let $b_2:f^*Rf_*\to Rp_{2*}p_1^*$ and $b_1:f^*Rf_*\to Rp_{1*}p_2^*$ be the canonical base-change mates [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Assume these and the projection maps used below are isomorphisms on $\mathcal L$ and that the displayed functors preserve $\mathcal L$. Take morphisms $t:Rf_*T_X\to R_Y$ and $t_i:Rp_{i*}T_W\to R_X$ satisfying $t_i\circ b_{i,T_X}=f^*t$ for $i=1,2$. Define $G(K)=f^*K\otimes T_X$ and
$$e_K=(1_K\otimes t)\circ\pi_{f,K,T_X}^{-1}:Rf_*GK\to K.$$
For $N\in\mathcal L(X)$ define the natural isomorphism
$$B_N:Rp_{2*}(p_1^*N\otimes T_W)\xrightarrow{\pi_{p_2,T_X,p_1^*N}^{-1}}Rp_{2*}p_1^*N\otimes T_X\xrightarrow{b_{2,N}^{-1}\otimes1}GRf_*N,$$
where the first arrow uses the canonical tensor symmetries.

For every $K\in\mathcal L(Y)$ one has
$$G(e_K)\circ B_{GK}=(1_{GK}\otimes t_2)\circ\pi_{p_2,GK,T_W}^{-1}.$$
Both sides have source $Rp_{2*}(p_1^*GK\otimes T_W)$ and target $GK$; on the right identify $p_1^*GK=p_2^*GK$ using $fp_1=fp_2$.

proof.text: Work in the ambient unbounded categories, and restrict at the end to the given full localizing subcategories. These are derived categories of sheaves over the commutative ring sheaves $R_Z$: [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] defines precisely the total module-derived functors, and [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] identifies module inverse image with exact inverse image. Thus the ringed-topos formulas apply to these actual functors, without replacing condensed coefficients by constant discrete coefficients or towers. The canonical pullback comparisons are symmetric monoidal and compatible with composition by [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons]. In particular $p_1^*f^*K=p_2^*f^*K$ and $p_1^*T_X=p_2^*T_X$ use the comparisons for $fp_1=fp_2$. In the rest of the proof put $r=p_2$, $R=Rr_*$, $a=f^*K$, $T=T_X$, $U=r^*a$, $V=r^*T=T_W$, and $S=RV$. Tensor associators and unitors are understood. The assumed preservation of $\mathcal L$ and invertibility of the displayed maps justify all subsequent inverses.

proof.text: The symmetry $\sigma_{V,V}$ is the identity. Indeed [sk-def-sp-tate-twist] states that $R_W(1)$ is pro-etale locally free of rank one. It is flat: on a trivializing cover tensoring is the identity, and exactness of a sequence of sheaves is checked locally. The complex with this sheaf in degree $-2$ and zero elsewhere is therefore K-flat by [lem-weil-pbc-independent-bounded-flat-kflat]. It represents $V=R_W(1)[2]$: the one-term complex $R_Y(1)[2]$ is K-flat by the same argument, so its derived pullbacks along $f$ and then $r=p_2$ are computed by module pullback of this complex [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], and module pullback of the twist is the twist by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients](1). By the representative formula in [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal], its tensor symmetry is the ordinary flip multiplied by $(-1)^{(-2)(-2)}=1$. On a trivializing cover, for a generator $z$ and local scalars $b,c$, the flip sends $bz\otimes cz$ to $cz\otimes bz=bc(z\otimes z)=bz\otimes cz$. Thus it is the identity as a morphism of sheaves, hence as a chain map before localization, and consequently in the derived category. This does not test equality of arbitrary derived maps by restriction to a cover. Since the symmetry is natural, the same holds for $\sigma$ of any two objects identified with $V$ by the canonical comparisons.

source.place: Tag 06YQ, lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat; signed tensor comparison of Tag 07A4; blueprint (1), the two (1)[2] factors in the second triangle

proof.text:
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence] to the square with $(f',g,g')=(p_2,f,p_1)$, taking its objects $(E,Q)=(T_X,K)$. Its exchange is exactly $b_2$, since both are the mate of the same pullback-composition comparison [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Its projection is initially written with the pushed-forward factor on the left. Conjugating source and target by tensor symmetry gives the left-factor convention of this item: their adjoint transposes are both $1\otimes c_h$ after the canonical pullback tensor comparison. Thus, with $b=b_2$, the cited square says
$$b_{GK}\circ f^*(\pi_{f,K,T})=\pi_{r,a,V}\circ(1_a\otimes b_T).$$
Here $p_1^*(f^*K\otimes T)=U\otimes V$. Set $\lambda=\pi_{r,a,V}:a\otimes S\to R(U\otimes V)$. The equation shows that $\lambda$ is an isomorphism, since $b_{GK}$, $b_T$ and $\pi_{f,K,T}$ are assumed isomorphisms. Inverting and multiplying the resulting equality gives
$$f^*(\pi_{f,K,T}^{-1})\circ b_{GK}^{-1}=(1_a\otimes b_T^{-1})\circ\lambda^{-1}.$$
This is an equality of the canonical maps, rather than a choice of projection-formula isomorphisms.

Let $H=R(U\otimes V\otimes V)$ and let
$$q:R(U\otimes V)\otimes T\longrightarrow H$$
be the right-factor projection map, namely the symmetry version of $\pi_{r,T,U\otimes V}$. By definition of $B$ we have $B_{GK}=(b_{GK}^{-1}\otimes1_T)q^{-1}$. Expanding $G(e_K)$, using the symmetric monoidal naturality of $f^*$ [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons], and inserting step 3 gives
$$G(e_K)B_{GK}=(1_a\otimes(f^*t\circ b_T^{-1})\otimes1_T)(\lambda^{-1}\otimes1_T)q^{-1}.$$
The assumed trace equation $t_2b_T=f^*t$ gives $f^*t\circ b_T^{-1}=t_2$. Consequently, for $D=(\lambda^{-1}\otimes1_T)q^{-1}:H\to a\otimes S\otimes T$,
$$G(e_K)B_{GK}=(1_a\otimes t_2\otimes1_T)D.$$
Only the equation for $t_2$ is needed; the unused equation for $t_1$ imposes no additional inference.

source.place: (1), second triangle: expand the counit and move the trace through base change

proof.text:
Put $\psi=\pi_{r,a\otimes T,V}:(a\otimes T)\otimes S\to H$. The tensor-action identity of [lem-sfb-ringed-projection-tensor-composition], applied with the two base factors $a,T$ and fibre factor $V$, gives, in the left/right conventions of steps 3 and 4,
$$q(\lambda\otimes1_T)=R(1_U\otimes\sigma_{V,V})\,\psi(1_a\otimes\sigma_{S,T}).$$
This is the cited identity $\pi_{r,E,Q\otimes T}=\pi_{r,E\otimes r^*Q,T}(\pi_{r,E,Q}\otimes1_T)$ with $(E,Q)=(V,a)$, followed by the tensor symmetries: the successive projections put the two fibre copies in the order $U,V_{\mathrm{old}},V_{\mathrm{new}}$, whereas the combined projection puts them in the order $U,V_{\mathrm{new}},V_{\mathrm{old}}$. The displayed $R(1_U\otimes\sigma_{V,V})$ is precisely this final transposition. Compatibility of the pullback comparisons with the symmetries is part of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons]. By step 2 the transposition is the identity, so inversion and cancellation give
$$\psi^{-1}=(1_a\otimes\sigma_{S,T})(\lambda^{-1}\otimes1_T)q^{-1}=(1_a\otimes\sigma_{S,T})D.$$
No new projection formula is asserted here: this is a two-factor substitution in the cited tensor-action law.

source.place: Tag 0B56, equation-projection-formula-map: tensor-action coherence of the projection mate; blueprint (1), exchange of the two Tate factors

proof.text:
Naturality of tensor symmetry for the morphism $t_2:S\to R_X$ gives
$$(1_T\otimes t_2)\sigma_{S,T}=\sigma_{R_X,T}(t_2\otimes1_T)=t_2\otimes1_T,$$
where unitors identify the last targets; this is naturality of the symmetry in [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal]. Hence steps 4 and 5 yield
$$G(e_K)B_{GK}=(1_a\otimes t_2\otimes1_T)D=(1_{a\otimes T}\otimes t_2)\psi^{-1}.$$
Since $a\otimes T=GK$ and $\psi=\pi_{p_2,GK,T_W}$, this is the claimed equality, with source $H=Rp_{2*}(p_1^*GK\otimes T_W)$ and target $GK$. The equality $p_1^*GK=p_2^*GK$ uses exactly the canonical comparisons fixed in step 1. The ambient identity restricts to $\mathcal L$ because all its objects and maps lie there by the stated assumptions.
